subject: NeuroScale compute reservation playbook & next actions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@neuroscale.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: NeuroScale compute reservation playbook & next actions

Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed playbook so we have a single source of truth going into procurement/engineering. I tried to capture the pains, goals, and the concrete asks we agreed on.

High-level pain & goals (from your notes):
- Data sensitivity for inference and auditability (research PHI in some flows).
- Need single-tenant isolation for production workloads; cannot run on shared noisy neighbors.
- Peak throughput target: ~1200 concurrent inference requests (batching expected) with P95 latency goal <= 200ms.
- Elastic burst tolerance during experiments but predictable baseline for model training inference.
- Clear traceability & retention for audit (30+ days), KMS integration required.

Proposed reservation & SLA targets we discussed:
- Reserved pool: equivalent of 8x A100-40GB GPUs (we can map exact SKU once infra is finalized).
- Bursting: additional on-demand capacity up to 50% of pool for controlled bursts.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant (VPC peering + private deployment option) with customer-managed KMS/HSM support.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime on reserved pool, 500ms fallback model path if primary pool is degraded.
- Ops: runbook + canary rollout & automated fallback to quantized model variant.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Technical deep-dive: Neha to run a 60–90 minute session with your infra team to validate network/KMS needs (target: week of Nov 16).
2) Procurement checklist: Thomas — we'll share a SOW template and invoice/PO expectations; please return procurement_requirements.xlsx by Nov 20.
3) Pilot timeline: agree pilot scope and acceptance criteria — target pilot start in Jan 2027, 6-week pilot.
4) Risk items: confirming HIPAA scoping for PHI paths and whether additional contractual terms are required.

Attachments: neuroscale_playbook_draft.pdf (draft playbook), sow_template_v2.docx (SOW skeleton).

If that matches your recollection, I'll kick off the deep-dive scheduling and loop in our solutions engineer for the network session.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(attachment: neuroscale_playbook_draft.pdf)
From: Dr. Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@neuroscale.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Thomas Blake <thomas.blake@procurement.neuroscale.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:04:23 -0600
Subject: Re: NeuroScale compute reservation playbook & next actions

Karthik — this is perfect, thanks for taking such detailed notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- KMS/HSM: NeuroScale requires customer keys (HSM-backed) for model encryption at rest and for the KV cache. Can your private deployment support BYOK with HSM integration (we have Thales)?
- Audit retention: we need immutable logs for 90 days for select datasets — can you confirm the retention policy and where logs are stored?
- SLA carve-outs: experiments team will want to know the exact ramp window and what constitutes an SLA incident (we're sensitive to warm-up delays).

I've attached our procurement template with our internal PO cadence and payment terms — please review. Also including a short note from our security lead about encryption expectations.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
VP of ML Ops, NeuroScale Therapeutics
(Attachment: procurement_requirements.xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@neuroscale.ai>, Thomas Blake <thomas.blake@procurement.neuroscale.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:37:12 -0800
Subject: Re: NeuroScale compute reservation playbook & next actions

Elena / Thomas — thanks, got the procurement template. Quick notes on your clarifications: 

- BYOK/HSM: yes — our Private deployment supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations (Thales and AWS CloudHSM tested). We'll have Neha validate the specific key rotation & access control patterns in the deep-dive.
- Audit retention: for reserved pools we keep append-only audit logs. Default retention is 90 days for security/audit bundles; longer retention can be added as a paid retention add-on. Logs are stored in your customer-owned S3 (or a managed retention bucket we provision) depending on your compliance policy.
- SLA details: we'll send an SLA appendix that defines incident windows, warm-up grace periods, and measurable SLOs for P99/P95 latency. For pilot we propose sample acceptance tests for throughput and cold-start behavior.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/NS-RED-2026-11 | DocuSign SOW skeleton: https://www.docusign.com/skeleton/NS-RED-SOW

Next: Neha — can you propose two slots next week for the network/KMS deep-dive with their infra/security?

Thanks —
Karthik
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:08 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: scaling & fallbacks for NeuroScale (runbook attached)

Internal note (do not forward to NeuroScale yet) —
Summary of technical approach for the reserved pool:
- Baseline: 8 GPU-equivalent reservation mapped to exact SKU after Neha's sizing.
- Autoscaling policy: continuous batching + two-tier autoscale: (1) intra-pool burst via capped local queue, (2) cross-pool spill to pre-approved overflow with lower-cost quantized model.
- Canary & rollout: 5% traffic canary for first 48 hours, rollback on error rate > 1.5% vs baseline.
- Fallback behavior: if primary pool CPU/GPU pressure > 85% for 10+ mins, route to fallback variant with relaxed latency target (P95 <= 500ms).
- Ops runbook attached: reserved_pool_runbook.md — includes health checks, escalation paths, and postmortem template.

I'll prepare the segment for the SLA appendix and hand it to Grace to route to leadership for exception approval.

Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer
(Attachment: reserved_pool_runbook.md)
